heading.purpose: Page titles: project name, Overview, empty state. 20px/600, −0.01em.

title.purpose: Card titles and section heads; dialog headings at 16px. 14px/600.

label.purpose: Meter labels, counts, metadata, table headers; captions 12px. 12.5px, values always tabular.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Top-layer surfaces only: native <dialog>, the task drawer, bar popovers. In-page surfaces never take a shadow.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing for every transition in the app.

motion.name: drawer
motion.purpose: Task drawer slide from the right.

motion.name: arrival
motion.purpose: Alarm-mark entry and in-column card slides (FLIP).

motion.name: flight
motion.purpose: Card flights between stage columns (FLIP via WAAPI).

motion.name: ramp
motion.purpose: Indicator fill ramps to new values.

motion.name: trace
motion.purpose: One-time mark trace when a card lands.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Everything collapses under prefers-reduced-motion except the spinner (0.7s); traces and slides do not run.

breakpoints.name: columns-2
breakpoints.purpose: Stage columns collapse 4 → 2 at this container width.

breakpoints.name: columns-1
breakpoints.purpose: Stage columns collapse to one; performance charts stack.

breakpoints.name: shell-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Viewport: the shell stacks, the area list becomes a horizontal strip, touch targets grow to 40px, inputs to 16px.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one steel-filled action per view: New task, Create release, dialog confirms.
components.css: .primary { min-height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; background: #8fb0d0; color: #14181d; font: 600 13.5px/1.35 "Segoe UI Variable Text", "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; } .primary:hover { background: #a6c2de; } .primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #a6c2de; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Task Card
components.description: The kanban unit; the whole card is the hit area. Landed (done) cards recede to panel stock.
components.css: .card { padding: 10px 12px; background: #3a3f45; border: 1px solid #3d4248; border-radius: 4px; color: #c9ced4; font-size: 14px; } .card:hover { background: #41464d; border-color: #4a5057; } .card.needs { border-color: #f0b429; } .card.done { background: #303338; font-weight: 500; }

components.name: Load Meter
components.description: 56×8 recessed indicator with a band-limit tick at 85%; fill is grey in band, amber above, red at critical.
components.css: .meter { position: relative; display: inline-block; width: 56px; height: 8px; background: #1f2225; border-radius: 3px; } .fill { position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; background: #8f979f; border-radius: 3px; transition: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 1); } .meter.high .fill { background: #f0b429; } .meter.crit .fill { background: #e5534b; } .tick { position: absolute; top: -1px; bottom: -1px; left: 85%; width: 1px; background: #4a5057; } .val { color: #eceef1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Stage Column Chart
components.description: Performance stage mix: one vertical bar per stage per project; the value on top and the stage label below carry the meaning, so the grey ramp never has to.

narrative.overview: Ottr is a control-room overview for coding agents, built as an ISA-101 high-performance HMI in dark. Grey means every agent runs as it should; colour appears only when a task needs the operator or the machine leaves its normal band. It deliberately refuses the category default — a GitHub-dark kanban where every column, badge, and chart is always coloured. The world is flat graphite: a work-area field under a darker chrome layer, panels and cards on 1px lines. There are no gradients, no glass, no glow. Values are brighter than labels and always tabular. Depth is not the signal — state is.
keyCharacteristics: All-grey board at rest; the first amber is the event
Redundant state coding: shape carries state, hue only severity
Analog indicators that show their own normal band
One steel-blue interaction/selection edge, nothing else
Flat 1px-line elevation; shadow only on top-layer overlays
Native platform surfaces: <dialog> top layer and Popover API
WCAG 2.1 AA is binding: contrast, visible focus, names, announced status

rules.name: The Grey-Is-Normal Rule
rules.body: Colour is an alarm channel. If a state is fine, it renders in grey; amber and red are reserved for needs-you and critical.

rules.name: The Redundant-Coding Rule
rules.body: No alarm state is carried by hue alone. Needs-you is an amber triangle, critical a red square, band exceedance a tick plus amber fill.

rules.name: The One-Edge Rule
rules.body: Steel blue is the only interactive colour. Hover states lighten greys or add the steel edge; they never introduce a second hue.

rules.name: The Values-Read-First Rule
rules.body: Data read at a glance uses bright text and tabular figures; labels stay dim.

rules.name: The Operator's-Frame Rule
rules.body: The overview bar and navigation hold position; only the work pane scrolls.

rules.name: The Shadow-Is-Overlayer Rule
rules.body: A shadow appears only where an element leaves the page layer: dialogs, the drawer, popovers.

rules.name: The Shape-Says-It Rule
rules.body: State marks are a closed set of five glyphs; new states pick a glyph, not a colour.

rules.name: The Native-Platform Rule
rules.body: Modality uses the platform: <dialog> for focus and Esc, the Popover API for light-dismiss detail. No JS re-implements what the browser ships.

rules.name: WCAG 2.1 AA Binding
rules.body: Contrast 4.5:1 / 3:1 including non-text boundaries, visible steel focus on every interactive element, names on icon-only controls, status in live regions, reflow at 320px, reduced-motion tiers, pointer-free alternative for drag.

dos: Do render every healthy state in grey, with bright tabular values for anything numeric.
Do pair every amber or red with its shape — triangle, square, or band tick.
Do keep the steel accent as the only interactive colour; one edge per screen for selection.
Do use native <dialog> and the Popover API for modality and light-dismiss detail.
Do let landed work recede: recessed stock, lighter title weight, no celebration.
Do keep all motion on the shared easing, and respect the reduced-motion tiers.
Do keep WCAG 2.1 AA: contrast, visible focus, names on icon-only controls, announced status.
donts: Don't colour charts, columns, badges, or counts that are not alarming — this is not a GitHub-dark kanban.
Don't add gradients, glass, blur, or glow; surfaces are flat fills on 1px lines.
Don't make alarms blink, pulse, or repeat; an alarm arrives once.
Don't put shadows on in-page surfaces; shadow means top-layer overlay.
Don't invent a second accent hue; links, focus, and selection are all the same steel.
Don't drop the redundant coding — a colour-only alarm fails the world and colour-blind operators alike.
Don't ship a UI change that fails WCAG 2.1 AA — a contrast, focus, name, or status-message regression is a defect.
